doc.heroTitle: COW Token V2 — Complete Guide to
doc.heroDesc: A collateral-backed stablecoin protocol. Deposit BNB, receive COW at 80% LTV, powered by Chainlink oracle pricing. Learn about minting, burning, collateral management, liquidation, fees, and anti-rug-pull safety.
doc.videoDemoDesc: Detailed video tutorial on how to connect your wallet, mint tokens, burn tokens, and manage assets on COW Stablecoin.
doc.prerequisitesText: Before you begin, ensure you have: (1) MetaMask browser extension installed from metamask.io. (2) Some BNB in your wallet for collateral deposits and gas fees. (3) Connected to BSC Testnet (Chain ID: 97) or BSC Mainnet (Chain ID: 56). The DApp will automatically prompt you to switch networks if needed.
doc.connectWalletText: Click the "Connect Wallet" button in the header. MetaMask will prompt you to approve the connection. Once connected, your wallet address, BNB balance, COW token balance, and collateral position will be displayed. The DApp uses read-only access — your private keys never leave MetaMask.
doc.howMintingWorksText: COW Token V2 uses a collateral-backed model similar to DAI/MakerDAO. When you mint COW tokens, you deposit BNB as collateral. The protocol calculates the USD value of your BNB using Chainlink's real-time BNB/USD oracle price, then applies an 80% Loan-to-Value (LTV) ratio to determine how many COW tokens you receive. Each COW token is pegged to $1 USD. For example: depositing 1 BNB at $600 BNB/USD gives you $600 × 80% = $480 worth of COW tokens (before fees).
doc.stepsToMintText: 1. Enter the BNB amount you wish to deposit as collateral. 2. The DApp shows a preview: COW tokens to receive, spread fee (1% → treasury), mint fee (0.3% → feeCollector), and your resulting collateral ratio. 3. Click "Mint Tokens" and approve the transaction in MetaMask. 4. Your BNB collateral is locked in the smart contract, and COW tokens are minted to your wallet. 5. Your position is recorded: collateral amount, COW minted, and health ratio. You can add more collateral anytime by minting again — positions accumulate.
doc.whatIsBurningText: Burning COW tokens is how you withdraw your BNB collateral. When you burn COW, the protocol calculates the proportional BNB share from your position and returns it minus fees. You can burn partially (redeem some collateral while keeping a position) or burn all your COW to close your position entirely. Important: you can only burn up to the COW amount you originally minted — transferred COW tokens cannot be used to claim someone else's collateral.
doc.stepsToBurnText: 1. Enter the COW amount you wish to burn. 2. Preview shows: BNB to receive, spread fee (1% → treasury), burn fee (0.3% → feeCollector). 3. Click "Burn Tokens" and approve in MetaMask. 4. COW tokens are burned, your position is updated, and net BNB is returned to your wallet. Full burns clear your position entirely. Partial burns reduce your collateral and COW minted proportionally. Your collateral ratio remains the same after partial burns.
doc.contractArchText: COWToken V2 is built on Solidity 0.8.24 using OpenZeppelin's ERC20, Ownable, ReentrancyGuard, and Pausable contracts. Key components: (1) Chainlink AggregatorV3Interface for real-time BNB/USD price oracle with staleness checks (max 1 hour). (2) Per-user CollateralPosition tracking (BNB deposited + COW minted). (3) Configurable parameters: LTV (max 90%), spread fee, mint/burn fees (max 5% each), liquidation threshold. (4) Auto-liquidation with 5% penalty for liquidators. (5) Anti-rug-pull: NO admin withdraw() or mint() functions — collateral only leaves via user burns or liquidations.
doc.auditSecurityText: COW Token V2 is designed with maximum user protection: ① No admin can withdraw collateral — BNB only leaves the contract through burns or liquidations. ② No admin can arbitrarily mint tokens — COW is only created when backed by collateral. ③ ReentrancyGuard prevents reentrancy attacks on mint/burn/liquidate. ④ Pausable allows emergency stops without risk to user funds. ⑤ All admin functions are controlled by Timelock (COWTimelock) for time-delayed governance changes. ⑥ Oracle staleness check prevents use of outdated prices (max 1 hour). ⑦ All contracts are open-source and verified on BscScan.
doc.supportedNetworksText: COW Token V2 is deployed on BSC networks with Chainlink price feeds. The DApp supports multiple EVM chains and will automatically detect your MetaMask network.
doc.faq1A: COW Token V2 is a collateral-backed stablecoin pegged to $1 USD. Users deposit BNB as collateral and receive COW tokens at 80% Loan-to-Value ratio, similar to how DAI works with MakerDAO. The price is determined by Chainlink's decentralized BNB/USD oracle.
doc.faq2Q: What happens if BNB price drops significantly?
doc.faq2A: If BNB price drops and your collateral ratio falls below 105% (liquidation threshold), your position becomes eligible for liquidation. Anyone can liquidate your position — they repay your COW debt, receive a 5% penalty reward in BNB, and the remaining collateral is returned to you. To avoid liquidation, you can add more collateral by minting additional COW or partially burn COW to reduce your debt.
doc.faq3A: There are two types of fees: (1) Spread fee: 1% on mint/burn, sent to treasury2 for protocol development and reserves. (2) Mint/Burn fee: 0.3% each, sent to feeCollector for admin and developer maintenance. All fee parameters are configurable by the Timelock owner with a maximum cap of 5%.
doc.faq4Q: Can the admin steal my collateral?
doc.faq4A: No. The contract has NO withdraw() function for admin and NO arbitrary mint() function. Your BNB collateral can only leave the contract through two mechanisms: (1) You burn COW tokens to redeem your collateral. (2) Your position is liquidated when undercollateralized. Admin can only pause/unpause the contract, update fee parameters (capped at 5%), and change addresses — all through Timelock governance.
doc.faq5Q: How is the BNB/USD price determined?
doc.faq5A: The protocol uses Chainlink's decentralized oracle network (AggregatorV3Interface) for BNB/USD price feeds. The price is validated for freshness (must be updated within the last hour) and positivity (must be > 0). This ensures fair and tamper-proof pricing for minting, burning, and liquidation calculations.
doc.faq6A: LTV determines how many COW tokens you receive relative to your collateral's USD value. At 80% LTV: depositing $600 worth of BNB lets you mint $480 worth of COW. This over-collateralization (125% collateral ratio) protects the protocol and other users from price volatility. The LTV can be adjusted by governance (max 90%).
doc.faq7Q: Can I transfer COW tokens to others?
doc.faq7A: Yes, COW is a standard ERC-20 token. You can freely transfer, trade, or use COW tokens on DEXes. However, transferred COW cannot be used to claim someone else's collateral — only the original depositor can burn against their own position.
doc.bscFaucetText: To test COW Token V2 on BSC Testnet, you need free test BNB (tBNB) for collateral deposits and gas fees. Use the official BNB Chain Testnet Faucet below.

smartContract.s8_1R1_process: Send command via Timelock → Wait 48h → Execute

smartContract.s8_1Info: Important: Most daily changes (fee adjustments, LTV, emergency pause...) are Parameter changes — only need to send commands via Timelock, NO need to deploy a new contract.
smartContract.s8_2Text: All parameter changes on COWToken must go through the Timelock system (COWTimelock). Admin CANNOT make instant changes, must wait at least 48 hours.
smartContract.s8_2Step1: Schedule — Admin submits upgrade command to Timelock. Command is recorded on-chain, publicly visible to the entire community. Command is NOT YET effective.
smartContract.s8_2Step2:
Wait 48h — System holds the command for 48 hours. During this time:
• Everyone can view pending commands on BscScan
• Users check source code + smart contract to evaluate
• If signs of rug-pull → users Burn tokens + withdraw BNB before command takes effect
• Admin can cancel command if vulnerabilities or errors are found
smartContract.s8_2Step3: Execute — After 48h, admin can execute the command. If not executed, command expires automatically.
smartContract.s8_3Text: All admin parameters can be changed — each change must go through Timelock 48h:
smartContract.s8_3Warn: Hard-coded protection: Smart contract has hard-coded maximum limits. Fees CANNOT exceed 5%, LTV CANNOT exceed 90%. No one can change this, not even admin.

smartContract.s8_5R1_action: Check BscScan → Burn COW + withdraw BNB before 48h
smartContract.s8_5R2_action: Check new oracle → Withdraw assets if suspicious

smartContract.s9_1Text: A position can be liquidated when the collateral ratio drops below the liquidation threshold of 105% (10500 bps). This happens when the BNB price drops significantly, causing the collateral value to insufficiently back the minted COW.
smartContract.s9_1Formula1: Collateral Ratio = (Collateral BNB × BNB Price) ÷ COW Minted × 10000
smartContract.s9_1Formula2: Example: User deposits 1 BNB ($600) → Mints 480 COW. If BNB drops to $500 → Ratio = (1 × 500) ÷ 480 × 10000 = 10416 bps ≈ 104.16% → Eligible for liquidation!
smartContract.s9_1R2_action: Should add collateral or burn some COW
smartContract.s9_2Text: Process for liquidating an undercollateralized position on the smart contract:
smartContract.s9_2S1: Check position — Call getPosition(userAddress) or getCollateralRatio(userAddress) to check the collateral ratio
smartContract.s9_2S2: Verify conditions — Collateral ratio must be < 10500 bps (105%). If ratio ≥ 105%, transaction will revert with PositionHealthy error
smartContract.s9_2S3: Call liquidate() — Send transaction: contract.liquidate(userAddress). No BNB required, no approval needed
smartContract.s9_2S4: Receive reward — Liquidator receives 5% collateral of the liquidated position in BNB, automatically transferred to wallet
smartContract.s9_2S5: Result — User's COW tokens are burned, position is cleared, remaining BNB (95%) returned to user
smartContract.s9_3Title: 9.3 Code Example — Calling Liquidate from Frontend
smartContract.s9_3Text: Using ethers.js v6 to check and call liquidation:
smartContract.s9_3Warn: Note: The liquidate() function will revert if the position is healthy (ratio ≥ 105%). Always check getCollateralRatio() before calling to avoid losing gas fees.
smartContract.s9_4Reward2: Reward paid in BNB, automatically transferred to liquidator's wallet
smartContract.s9_4Reward3: No capital required — only gas fee for the transaction
smartContract.s9_4Risk1: Lost gas fee — If position was already liquidated by someone else or ratio recovered before tx confirms
smartContract.s9_4Risk2: Front-running — MEV bots may monitor mempool and liquidate before you
smartContract.s9_4Risk3: Oracle price delay — Price feed update delays may cause ratio to change quickly
smartContract.s9_4ExampleText: User has position: 1 BNB collateral, 480 COW minted. BNB drops to $490 → ratio = 102%. Liquidator calls liquidate() → Receives 0.05 BNB (5% × 1 BNB) ≈ $24.50. User receives back 0.95 BNB, 480 COW burned.
smartContract.s9_5Text: To find positions eligible for liquidation, you can use the following methods:
smartContract.s9_5Method1Text: Listen for Minted events to get a list of all users with positions, then check getCollateralRatio() for each user:
smartContract.s9_5Method2Text: Visit the Wallet page of the DApp, connect your wallet, and view the dashboard to monitor collateral ratios. When BNB price fluctuates significantly, check positions near the liquidation threshold.
smartContract.s9_5Info: Important note: The liquidation system is decentralized — anyone can participate. This mechanism ensures the COW Token system is always fully collateralized. Liquidators serve as system guardians and are rewarded accordingly for this action.

smartContract.s10_4Title: 10.4 Method 2: Manual Verification via BscScan Web
smartContract.s10_4Text: If Hardhat CLI fails, you can verify manually through the web interface:
smartContract.s10_4S1: Open BscScan → enter contract address → Contract tab → click "Verify and Publish"
smartContract.s10_4S5: Paste the entire source code (flatten if needed: npx hardhat flatten)
smartContract.s10_4S6: Enter Constructor Arguments (ABI-encoded) — copy from BscScan "Contract Creation" tab or use an encode tool
smartContract.s10_4S7: Click "Verify and Publish" → wait for BscScan to compile and match bytecode
smartContract.s10_4Warn: Note: Manual verification is error-prone due to compiler version and optimization settings mismatches. Hardhat CLI is recommended to avoid mistakes.

smartContract.s10_5Method1: 📋 Method 1: Copy from BscScan — open the deploy transaction → Input Data tab → the end part (after bytecode) is the constructor args
smartContract.s10_5Method2: 📋 Method 2: Use an encode script — create an arguments.js file and run it to get the ABI hex
